assertion.description: Heterozygous de novo truncating SMC1A variants, X-linked. assertion.name: DEE114
assertion.description: De novo missense SLC32A1 variants. SLC32A1 encodes the vesicular GABA transporter, which loads GABA into synaptic vesicles, so the lesion is presynaptic and inhibitory. Inherited missense variants in the same gene had already been linked to genetic epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, and this report establishes that de novo missense variants instead cause a DEE. Two mechanisms were demonstrated in a murine neuronal culture model: three variants lining the putative GABA transport pathway reduced quantal size, consistent with impaired vesicle filling, while an N-terminal variant left quantal size intact but raised presynaptic release probability.

selected_evidence.snippet: The main phenotype comprises moderate-to-severe intellectual disability, infantile-onset epilepsy within the first 18 months of life, and a choreiform, dystonic, or dyskinetic movement disorder.

assertion.name: DEE108
assertion.description: De novo MAST3 missense variants in the serine-threonine kinase domain. MAST3 is one of the microtubule-associated serine-threonine kinases, expressed in excitatory cortical neurons late in prenatal development and postnatally. All eleven individuals of the defining series had DEE, eight with normal development before seizure onset under two years of age, and fever-triggered and drug-resistant seizures in nine each. Transfected cells showed generally lower MAST3 expression with increased phosphorylation of its target ARPP-16, which the authors suggest may confer gain of function.

selected_evidence.snippet: All patients developed multiple seizure types, 9 of 11 patients had seizures triggered by fever and 9 of 11 patients had drug-resistant seizures.

assertion.description: Heterozygous, almost always de novo, missense or in-frame TMEM63B variants affecting conserved transmembrane residues. TMEM63B encodes a stretch-activated ion channel, and the mutated channels carried an inward leak cation current even under isotonic conditions while responding poorly to a hypo-osmotic challenge. Two features set this subtype apart from the other channel subtypes here: the brain changes are progressive and neurodegenerative rather than static, and haematological abnormalities such as macrocytosis and haemolysis occurred in twelve of seventeen individuals, some needing transfusion. The recurrent p.Val44Met accounted for seven of the seventeen.

assertion.description: Biallelic LGI1 variants - the recessive counterpart of the dominant LGI1 disease, autosomal dominant epilepsy with auditory features, which dismech curates as the separate Autosomal_Dominant_Epilepsy_with_Auditory_Features entry. assertion.name: DEE61

selected_evidence.snippet: All affected individuals exhibited infantile-onset, treatment-resistant epilepsy.

assertion.name: AR Complex HSP
assertion.display_name: Autosomal Recessive Complex Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia
assertion.description: Autosomal recessive forms of complex HSP, the group most strongly associated with thin corpus callosum and progressive cognitive decline. SPG11 (spatacsin) is the most common form and is characteristically associated with thin corpus callosum, intellectual disability/cognitive decline, peripheral neuropathy, and pseudobulbar involvement. SPG15 (ZFYVE26/spastizin) causes complicated autosomal-recessive spastic paraplegia including Kjellin syndrome (with pigmentary maculopathy). SPG7 (paraplegin) frequently presents with cerebellar ataxia and optic atrophy reflecting mitochondrial dysfunction. Additional characteristic autosomal recessive complex forms include SPG35 (FA2H, with leukodystrophy, seizures, and intellectual disability), SPG20/Troyer syndrome (SPART/spartin, with distal amyotrophy, dysarthria, and short stature), and the AP-4-associated HSP disorders (AP4B1/AP4M1/AP4E1/AP4S1; SPG47/50/51/52), a childhood-onset complex form with severe developmental delay and microcephaly.

selected_evidence.snippet: the identification of ZFYVE26, which encodes a zinc-finger protein with a FYVE domain that we named spastizin, as the cause of SPG15

assertion.name: FRAXE
assertion.description: CCG repeat expansion and consequent methylation-mediated silencing of AFF2 (FMR2) at the FRAXE folate-sensitive fragile site in Xq28. Mechanistically the repeat-expansion member of the class and the closest non-syndromic counterpart to fragile X syndrome, from which it is distinguished by a milder cognitive phenotype without the fragile X somatic features. AFF2 is among the genes found in non-syndromal families that were never assigned an IDX number.

selected_evidence.snippet: FRAXA expansion results in fragile X syndrome due to down regulation of expression of the FMR1 gene

assertion.name: MRX104
assertion.description: Deleterious FRMPD4 variants - an exon deletion, a nonsense change, a frameshift and a conserved-residue missense - in ten affected males from four unrelated families. FRMPD4 is a neural scaffolding protein that binds PSD-95 to promote dendritic spine morphogenesis and regulates mGluR1/5 signalling through Homer, so this subtype sits at the postsynaptic scaffold alongside DLG3. The frameshift allele disrupts binding to both PSD-95 and HOMER1 and fails to increase spine density in transfected hippocampal neurons, and knockout mice show hippocampus-dependent spatial learning deficits. Two qualifications belong on this row: the reporting authors describe the entity as a new X-linked intellectual disability syndrome, with language delay, seizures and behavioural or psychiatric disturbance alongside moderate-to-severe intellectual disability, and the ClinGen Intellectual Disability and Autism Gene Curation Expert Panel curates FRMPD4 as Definitive against "X-linked complex neurodevelopmental disorder" rather than against this class. OMIM and MONDO nonetheless number the entity within the non-syndromic series, and it is recorded here on that basis with the comorbidity stated rather than suppressed. A third point matters for the evidence audit this entry runs on itself: of the fourteen genes admitted in this enumeration pass, FRMPD4 is the only one named in either list that the 2013 reassessment against 10,563 control X chromosomes singles out, and it falls in the fifteen for which replication studies were warranted rather than in the ten whose involvement was questioned. Both reports cited on this row postdate that flag and supply the independent families it asked for.

selected_evidence.snippet: Clinical features of these patients consisted of moderate to severe ID, language delay and seizures alongside with behavioral and/or psychiatric disturbances.

assertion.name: MRX30
assertion.description: Truncating variants in PAK3 (p21-activated kinase) at Xq22, identified in the multiplex MRX30 pedigree. PAK3 couples Rho family GTPases to actin cytoskeletal reorganisation in postmitotic cortical and hippocampal neurons, and this subtype anchors the Rho GTPase theme that recurs across the class. MRI was normal in affected individuals - the imaging correlate of a functional rather than structural lesion.

selected_evidence.snippet: MRI analysis showed no gross defects in brain development.

assertion.name: IDX112
assertion.description: Protein-altering variants in ZMYM3, a transcriptional coregulator and component of the KDM1A-RCOR1 chromatin-modifying complex, in a MatchMaker Exchange cohort of 27 individuals - the largest cohort behind any row in this entry. Almost all variants are missense, several recurring at the same two residues, and a ChIP-seq experiment on one of them shows dramatically reduced genomic occupancy consistent with a hypomorphic effect. This places the subtype in the transcriptional-control theme alongside ARX and ZNF711 rather than at the synapse. The reported phenotype includes developmental delay, intellectual disability and behavioural abnormalities, with a specific facial gestalt in a subset of males only; the authors state that they cannot perform statistical evaluations to definitively support causation and rest the case on the totality of the evidence, and ZMYM3 has no ClinGen gene-disease validity curation.

selected_evidence.snippet: Overlapping features included developmental delay, intellectual disability, behavioral abnormalities, and a specific facial gestalt in a subset of males.

assertion.name: MRX21
assertion.description: Deletions and loss-of-function point variants in IL1RAPL1 at Xp22.1-21.3, encoding an interleukin-1 receptor accessory protein family member highly expressed in postnatal hippocampus. The founding report explicitly describes patients with cognitive impairment only, one of the clearest original descriptions in the class - though see the caveat below on later families. IL1RAPL1 is understood to act in excitatory synapse formation, though the cited primary report establishes only its hippocampal expression and infers a role in memory and learning. Later series identified behavioural problems and mild dysmorphism in some families, illustrating the instability of the non-syndromic label.

selected_evidence.snippet: Its high level of expression in post-natal brain structures involved in the hippocampal memory system suggests a specialized role for this new gene in the physiological processes underlying memory and learning abilities.

assertion.name: MRX41
assertion.description: Missense and null variants in GDI1, encoding alpha-GDI (Rab GDP dissociation inhibitor), which recycles Rab GTPases for synaptic vesicle traffic; the L92P allele reduces RAB3A binding and recycling. One of the purest non-syndromic exemplars in the class - a large German multiplex family had neither abnormal body measurements nor any other significant clinical problem, and the authors concluded that a clinical diagnosis of GDI1-associated disease is impossible.

selected_evidence.snippet: the affected male family members had nonsyndromic intellectual disability, that is, they had neither abnormal body measurements nor any other significant clinical problems

assertion.name: MRX19
assertion.description: The attenuated, non-syndromic arm of the RPS6KA3 (RSK2) allelic series, whose severe arm is Coffin-Lowry syndrome - curated separately in dismech as Coffin-Lowry_Syndrome (MONDO:0010561). RSK2 is a serine-threonine kinase, and the variants reported in this arm are single-amino-acid deletions and a missense change in the protein's proximal domain, similar in kind to Coffin-Lowry alleles; two of the three reported families had been given a non-syndromic clinical diagnosis, and in the third Coffin-Lowry had been suspected but the features were atypical and the intellectual disability much milder than expected. The clinically important consequence, and the reason the row is worth modelling separately, is diagnostic: the reporting authors conclude that strict reliance on classical clinical criteria for mutation testing may result in a missed diagnosis. ClinGen's Intellectual Disability and Autism Gene Curation Expert Panel curates RPS6KA3 only against Coffin-Lowry syndrome, so this arm has no separate expert-panel classification.

selected_evidence.snippet: In two families, the clinical diagnosis had been nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation.

assertion.name: MRX108
assertion.description: A recurrent missense variant (p.Leu515Phe) in the alkali cation/proton exchanger SLC9A7, segregating with multigenerational non-syndromic intellectual disability in two unrelated families. SLC9A7 resides in the trans-Golgi network and post-Golgi vesicles; the mutant protein is correctly targeted but alkalinises those compartments and impairs N-linked oligosaccharide maturation of exported cargo, which the authors read as a gain of function. Unusually for a class defined by the absence of biochemical features, it comes with a laboratory readout: patient sera show an abnormal transferrin N-glycosylation profile, the standard diagnostic marker for congenital disorders of glycosylation. SLC9A7 has no ClinGen gene-disease validity curation.

selected_evidence.snippet: This correlated with alkalinization of the TGN/post-Golgi compartments, suggestive of a gain-of-function.

assertion.name: MRX72
assertion.description: Null alleles of RAB39B, a neuronal-specific small GTPase of the Golgi compartment, identified in two male patients - one of them in the MRX72 family, where a 5' splice-site change abolished normal splicing. Its downregulation alters neurite growth cone number and morphology and reduces presynaptic boutons, placing the subtype in the vesicular trafficking theme. assertion.name: CEP83-related

selected_evidence.snippet: The distal appendages (DAPs) of centrioles are involved in the docking and anchoring of the mother centriole to the cellular membrane during ciliogenesis.

assertion.name: ZNF423-related

selected_evidence.snippet: ZNF423 | HGNC:16762 | ciliopathy | MONDO:0005308 | AR | Moderate

assertion.name: GLIS2-related

selected_evidence.snippet: GLIS2 | HGNC:29450 | nephronophthisis 7 | MONDO:0012680 | AR | Moderate

assertion.name: MAPKBP1-related

selected_evidence.snippet: MAPKBP1 | HGNC:29536 | nephronophthisis 20 | MONDO:0014997 | AR | Definitive

assertion.name: Infantile Nephronophthisis
assertion.description: Early onset in infancy characterized by rapid progression to end-stage renal disease.

selected_evidence.snippet: Infantile nephronophtisis is a recessive autosomic tubulo-interstitial nephritis with cortical microcysts which progress to end stage renal failure before age 5.

assertion.name: Adolescent Nephronophthisis

selected_evidence.snippet: Adolescent nephronophtisis is a less frequent form of nephronophtisis.

assertion.name: SPG72
assertion.description: HSP caused by variants in REEP2 (previous symbol C5orf19, HGNC read 2026-09-25), a gene closely related to the SPG31 gene REEP1. The original report identified a heterozygous missense allele segregating in an autosomal dominant family and a missense allele in trans with a splice-site allele in an autosomal recessive family, so both modes of inheritance are recorded. A later de novo missense allele in a patient with pure HSP was only the second autosomal dominant SPG72 missense mutation described. MONDO's editor note on this class records that it covers either dominant or recessive inheritance because Orphanet classifies SPG72 as both.

selected_evidence.snippet: The missense substitution p.Phe72Tyr, in the recessive family, decreased the affinity of the mutant protein for membranes that, together with the splice site mutation, is expected to cause complete loss of REEP2 function.

assertion.name: SPG62
assertion.description: Autosomal recessive HSP caused by biallelic variants in ERLIN1 (previous symbols C10orf69 and SPFH1, HGNC read 2026-09-25). ClinGen grades the relationship as Definitive and lumps ERLIN1-related amyotrophic lateral sclerosis into the same disease entity, noting that SPG62 can convert to ALS. A splice-site allele reported in the first Chinese patient caused delayed-onset pure HSP.

selected_evidence.snippet: It is recognized that HSP62 can convert to ALS.

assertion.name: SPG31
assertion.description: Autosomal dominant HSP caused by variants in REEP1, an endoplasmic reticulum-shaping protein. Of the 16 mutations identified in a screen of 535 unrelated HSP patients, twelve were small insertions, deletions or splice-site changes predicted to shift the reading frame and cause haploinsufficiency, which that study established as the main molecular genetic mechanism in SPG31. Most patients present with a pure spastic paraplegia, with rare complicating features restricted to symptoms or signs of peripheral nerve involvement.

selected_evidence.snippet: Clinically most SPG31 patients present with a pure spastic paraplegia; rare complicating features were restricted to symptoms or signs of peripheral nerve involvement.

assertion.name: SPG3A
assertion.description: Autosomal dominant HSP caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in ATL1, encoding atlastin-1, a dynamin-like GTPase that mediates homotypic fusion of endoplasmic reticulum tubules. SPG3A is the most common cause of early childhood-onset autosomal dominant HSP, with average age of onset around four years and a relatively slow, often non-progressive course. Usually a pure HSP, but complicated forms with axonal motor neuropathy and distal amyotrophy (Silver syndrome phenotype) occur.

selected_evidence.snippet:
The average age of onset is four years. More 
than 80% of reported individuals manifest spastic gait before the end of the 
first decade of life.

assertion.name: SPG80
assertion.description: Autosomal dominant juvenile-onset pure HSP caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in UBAP1 (previous symbol UBAP, HGNC read 2026-09-25). The reported alleles were identified in four families of the Japan Spastic Paraplegia Research Consortium, and a C-terminal deletion mutant lost ubiquitin binding in vitro and could not be recruited to endosome membranes.

selected_evidence.snippet: All the patients presented identical clinical features of a pure type of juvenile-onset HSP.

assertion.name: SPG83
assertion.description: Autosomal recessive HSP caused by biallelic variants in HPDL (previous symbol GLOXD1, HGNC read 2026-09-27), which encodes a putative iron-containing non-heme oxygenase that localises to mitochondria. In the series of 25 families that established the gene, phenotypes ranged from juvenile-onset pure hereditary spastic paraplegia to infantile-onset spasticity with global developmental delay, so one gene accounts for both pure and complex presentations; the juvenile-onset pure presentation is the reason this subtype is recorded here. A later patient-registry study separates the spectrum into severe, intermediate and mild classes with onset in early infancy, childhood and adolescence respectively, and correlates biallelic truncating genotypes with the severe end.

selected_evidence.snippet: We establish three major clinical classes: severe, intermediate, and mild, presenting onset in early infancy, childhood, and adolescence, respectively.

assertion.name: SPG8

ClinGen grades the WASHC5 relationship to hereditary spastic paraplegia 8 as Moderate, and splits it from the autosomal recessive Ritscher-Schinzel syndrome 1 relationship of the same gene on grounds of inheritance pattern and clinical phenotype; WASHC5 is bound in this knowledge base's Ritscher-Schinzel syndrome entries for that second relationship.

assertion.name: SPG4
assertion.description: Autosomal dominant HSP caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in SPAST, encoding the microtubule-severing AAA ATPase spastin. SPG4 is the single most common form of autosomal dominant HSP and is the prototype of pure HSP, though dementia, ataxia, thin corpus callosum, and muscle wasting have been reported. Onset is insidious, mostly in young adulthood, with considerable intrafamilial variation.

selected_evidence.snippet:
Spastic paraplegia 4 (SPG4; also known as SPAST-HSP)

spasticity.

assertion.name: SPG11
assertion.description: Autosomal recessive complex HSP caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in SPG11, encoding spatacsin. SPG11 is one of the most common forms of autosomal recessive HSP and is characteristically associated with thinning of the corpus callosum, mild intellectual disability or progressive cognitive decline, peripheral neuropathy, and pseudobulbar involvement. Onset is usually in infancy or adolescence, and most affected individuals become wheelchair-bound one or two decades after onset.

selected_evidence.snippet:
Spastic paraplegia 11 (SPG11) is characterized by 
progressive spasticity and weakness of the lower limbs frequently associated 
with the following: mild intellectual disability with learning difficulties in 
childhood and/or progressive cognitive decline; peripheral neuropathy; 
pseudobulbar involvement; and increased reflexes in the upper limbs.

subtype_term.preferred_term: frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis 1

term.label: frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis 1

assertion.description: The chromosome 9p-linked FTD/ALS locus, caused by a noncoding GGGGCC hexanucleotide repeat expansion in C9orf72 rather than by a coding lesion. In European populations it is the commonest genetic cause of both familial ALS and familial FTD. It is the largest of several shared causes, not the only one: TBK1, CCNF and VCP are likewise numbered as FTD and/or ALS loci in the rows below, and TARDBP and UBQLN2 also span ALS and dementia. The ranking does not hold everywhere either: in Asian populations SOD1 is the commonest ALS gene and C9orf72 expansions are comparatively rare.

selected_evidence.snippet: The clinical presentation is highly heterogeneous and may differ between and within families, causing an unpredictable pattern and age of onset of clinical manifestations.

selected_evidence.snippet: Mutations of the lipid phosphatase FIG4 that regulates PI(3,5)P(2) are responsible for the recessive peripheral-nerve disorder CMT4J.

assertion.description: The numbered form caused by haploinsufficiency of BICRA (also GLTSCR1), which encodes a subunit of the non-canonical BAF (ncBAF) complex rather than of canonical BAF. assertion.name: CSS4
assertion.description:
The SMARCA4-related form of Coffin-Siris syndrome, corresponding to OMIM 614609. SMARCA4 encodes BRG1, the catalytic ATPase subunit of the BAF/PBAF chromatin-remodelling complex - so this is the subtype in which the motor of the complex is damaged rather than one of its scaffolding or targeting subunits.
The subtype carries two names for one concept, and the second name is the informative one. assertion.name: Harlequin Ichthyosis
assertion.description: Severe ARCI phenotype, most often linked to ABCA12 loss-of-function, with profound neonatal hyperkeratosis and barrier compromise. The neonate is encased in thick plate-like armour separated by deep fissures, with ectropion, eclabium and flattened ears. It is no longer invariably fatal: with modern neonatal care, reported survival is around half, and deaths concentrate in the first three months from sepsis and respiratory failure - the direct consequences of a stratum corneum that cannot function as a barrier. Survivors carry a chronic severe scaling erythroderma. Genotype tracks outcome, with homozygous loss-of-function alleles reported in all deaths in the largest series and compound heterozygosity over-represented among survivors. The reported association between early oral retinoid treatment and survival in that series is deliberately not curated here as a treatment effect: it is a retrospective, questionnaire-based comparison with no randomisation and obvious scope for confounding by indication and by era of neonatal care, and the source itself claims only that early retinoids may improve survival.

selected_evidence.snippet: The most severe form of ARCI, harlequin ichthyosis, is caused by mutations in ABCA12.

selected_evidence.snippet: With the 2019 breakthrough in the development of highly effective modulator therapy providing unprecedented clinical benefits for over 90% of patients with cystic fibrosis who are genetically eligible for treatment, this rare disease has become a front runner of transformative molecular therapy.

assertion.name: SIM1
assertion.description: Severe obesity caused by loss-of-function variants in SIM1, a bHLH-PAS transcription factor with a key role in neuronal differentiation in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus, where MC4R is also expressed. Alleles with strong loss of function segregate with a high intra-family risk of obesity, and mouse Sim1 haploinsufficiency produces resistance to hypothalamic melanocortin signaling, which places this gene in the same pathway as the receptor-level and ligand-level subtypes rather than beside them. Severe obesity occurs both with and without Prader-Willi-like features. Contiguous 6q16 deletions that remove SIM1 together with neighbouring genes are a separate disease and are curated as 6q16_Deletion_Syndrome; this subtype is the intragenic form.

selected_evidence.snippet: Three mutations showed strong loss-of-function effects (p.T46R, p.H323Y, and p.T714A) and were associated with high intra-family risk for obesity, while the variants with mild or no effects on SIM1 activity were not associated with obesity within families.
